items.readable_text:
Content:
When we round a number to the nearest whole number, we find the closest whole number to our number.

Content:
Rounding a number to the nearest whole number is often useful when dividing two whole numbers with remainders.

Content:
To demonstrate, let's round the result of the following division problem to the nearest whole number:

Content:
[MATH: 79 \div 6]

Content:
We start by going through the long division procedure as usual:

Content:
| | | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 3] | / | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: \!\!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{7 {\:\phantom{|}} 9 }] | / | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 6] | | / | | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 9] | / | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 8] | / | | | [MATH: 1] | |

Content:
So, [MATH: 79 \div 6 = 13 \, \textrm{R} \, 1.] Writing this result as a mixed number, we obtain

Content:
[MATH: 79 \div 6 = 13 \, {\color{blue}\dfrac{1}{6}}.]

Content:
We need to round this result to the nearest whole number. So, we need to decide whether to round down or round up.

Content:
Note that,

Content:
- rounding the answer down gives [MATH: 13,] while
- rounding the answer up gives [MATH: 14.]

Content:
To decide whether to round down or up, we need to decide which of these two options [MATH: (13] or [MATH: 14)] is closest to [MATH: 13 \, {\color{blue}\dfrac{1}{6}}.] To do this, we compare the fractional part of our answer to [MATH: {\color{red}\dfrac12}.]

Content:
Now, since
[MATH: {\color{blue}\dfrac{1}{6}} < {\color{red}\dfrac{1}{2}},]

Content:
this tells us that [MATH: 13 \, {\color{blue}\dfrac{1}{6}}] is closer to [MATH: 13] than to [MATH: 14.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/34fbac9df8d460b4bd8308e512a8c900]

Content:
Therefore, we need to round down:

Content:
[MATH: 13 \, {\color{blue}\dfrac{1}{6}} \to 13]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 79 \div 6] rounded to the nearest whole number is [MATH: 13.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
When we round a number to the nearest whole number, we find the closest whole number to our number.

Content:
Rounding a number to the nearest whole number is often useful when dividing two whole numbers with remainders.

Content:
To demonstrate, let's round the result of the following division problem to the nearest whole number:

Content:
[MATH: 79 \div 6]

Content:
We start by going through the long division procedure as usual:

Content:
| | | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 3] | / | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: \!\!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{7 {\:\phantom{|}} 9 }] | / | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 6] | | / | | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 9] | / | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 8] | / | | | [MATH: 1] | |

Content:
So, [MATH: 79 \div 6 = 13 \, \textrm{R} \, 1.] Writing this result as a mixed number, we obtain

Content:
[MATH: 79 \div 6 = 13 \, {\color{blue}\dfrac{1}{6}}.]

Content:
We need to round this result to the nearest whole number. So, we need to decide whether to round down or round up.

Content:
Note that,

Content:
- rounding the answer down gives [MATH: 13,] while
- rounding the answer up gives [MATH: 14.]

Content:
To decide whether to round down or up, we need to decide which of these two options [MATH: (13] or [MATH: 14)] is closest to [MATH: 13 \, {\color{blue}\dfrac{1}{6}}.] To do this, we compare the fractional part of our answer to [MATH: {\color{red}\dfrac12}.]

Content:
Now, since
[MATH: {\color{blue}\dfrac{1}{6}} < {\color{red}\dfrac{1}{2}},]

Content:
this tells us that [MATH: 13 \, {\color{blue}\dfrac{1}{6}}] is closer to [MATH: 13] than to [MATH: 14.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/34fbac9df8d460b4bd8308e512a8c900]

Content:
Therefore, we need to round down:

Content:
[MATH: 13 \, {\color{blue}\dfrac{1}{6}} \to 13]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 79 \div 6] rounded to the nearest whole number is [MATH: 13.]

Item 2 — Tutorial: Rules for Rounding Division Problems

Content:
When rounding the result of a division to the nearest whole number, we apply the following rules:

Content:
- When the fractional part is smaller than [MATH: \dfrac12,] we round down.
- When the fractional part is greater than or equal to [MATH: \dfrac12,] we round up.
